name: Sivers Semiconductors AB
title: Sivers Semiconductors — the laser chokepoint at the start of the curve
subtitle: How a Stockholm-listed InP DFB laser maker became the upstream pure-play in the co-packaged optics supply chain — and what its planned US dual listing implies
abstract: Sivers Semiconductors AB (SIVE.ST, Nasdaq Stockholm) is a 75-year-old Swedish-listed semiconductor group whose Glasgow-based photonics subsidiary has become the leading independent western source of custom InP DFB lasers for AI data-centre co-packaged optics. FY2025 revenue grew 25% (33% constant FX) to SEK 306.6M; the sales pipeline expanded 64% to $453M. A PCAOB-aligned restatement published on 13 May 2026 widened the operating loss to SEK 177.8M from the SEK 141.3M originally reported under Swedish K3, exposing less-conservative items being cleaned up ahead of a planned Nasdaq New York dual listing. CEO Vickram Vathulya (PhD Lehigh, MBA Berkeley Haas) was appointed August 2024 with a personal commitment to subscribe to up to $1M of stock; Executive Chairman Bami Bastani (42-year semiconductor veteran, three-time public-company turnaround CEO, ex-GlobalFoundries SVP) joined as Strategic Advisor in August 2023. Co-founder Erik Fällström — who controls ~11.8% of votes via DDM Debt — departs the board at the 15 June 2026 AGM, where shareholders also vote on a 15% dilution authority to fund the US listing. The stock has moved from SEK 1.80 to SEK 72.90 over five years and trades at its 5-year high; the market is pricing a co-packaged-optics production ramp that has not yet shipped.
